## Declarations and implementations

```plato
//==
// # Signals
//
// Sections, in order:
//  - Signals
//  - Signal filters and rate conversion
//  - Signal envelopes and generators

//==
// # Signals
//
// Uniformly sampled signals, frequency-domain representations, and the
// analysis windows that produce them. Conventions: sample i of a signal
// occurs at time i / SampleRate; spectrum bin k is centered at k * BinWidth
// with bin 0 at DC. Filters and rate conversion, and envelopes and generators,
// follow in the sections below.

// A uniformly sampled scalar signal. Sample i occurs at time i / SampleRate.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sampling_(signal_processing))
type SampledSignal
    implements IValue
{
    SampleRate: Frequency;
    Samples: Array<Number>;
}

// A uniformly sampled signal with multiple interleaved channels. Samples are
// frame-interleaved (all channels of frame 0, then frame 1, ...); the sample
// count is a multiple of ChannelCount.
type MultichannelSignal
    implements IValue
{
    SampleRate: Frequency;
    ChannelCount: Integer;
    Samples: Array<Number>;
}

// A single-sided magnitude/phase spectrum with uniform bins. Parallel arrays:
// bin k is centered at k * BinWidth (bin 0 is DC), with magnitude
// Magnitudes[k] and phase Phases[k].
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frequency_domain)
type Spectrum
    implements IValue
{
    BinWidth: Frequency;
    Magnitudes: Array<Number>;
    Phases: Array<Angle>;
}

// A complex-valued spectrum with uniform bins: Bins[k] holds the amplitude
// and phase of the component at k * BinWidth as one complex number.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discrete_Fourier_transform)
type ComplexSpectrum
    implements IValue
{
    BinWidth: Frequency;
    Bins: Array<Complex>;
}

// A time-frequency magnitude map from a short-time transform. The column
// index of Magnitudes selects the time frame (frame j starts at j * TimeStep)
// and the row index selects the frequency bin (bin k at k * BinWidth).
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spectrogram)
type Spectrogram
    implements IValue
{
    TimeStep: Duration;
    BinWidth: Frequency;
    Magnitudes: Array2D<Number>;
}

//==
// # Analysis windows

// The taper shape applied to a block of samples before spectral analysis.
// The parameter-carrying kinds hold their own shape parameter; the parameter-
// free kinds carry none.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Window_function)
type WindowFunction
    implements IValue
    = Rectangular
    | Hann
    | Hamming
    | Blackman
    | BlackmanHarris
    | Kaiser(Beta: Number)                    // the Kaiser beta
    | Gaussian(StandardDeviation: Number)     // standard deviation, in samples
    | Tukey(TaperFraction: Proportion);       // fraction of the window that is tapered

// A short-time analysis configuration. Size is the window length in samples;
// HopSize is the advance between consecutive windows.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Short-time_Fourier_transform)
type AnalysisWindow
    implements IValue
{
    Function: WindowFunction;
    Size: Integer;
    HopSize: Integer;
}

//==
// # Derived representations

// An analytic (Hilbert) representation of a real signal: parallel in-phase
// and quadrature sample arrays, from which instantaneous amplitude and
// phase follow.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Analytic_signal)
type AnalyticSignal
    implements IValue
{
    SampleRate: Frequency;
    InPhase: Array<Number>;
    Quadrature: Array<Number>;
}

// An inclusive band of frequencies from Low to High: equalizer bands,
// octave analysis, band-limited processing.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frequency_band)
type FrequencyBand
    implements IValue
{
    Low: Frequency;
    High: Frequency;
}

//==
// # Signal filters and rate conversion
//
// Digital filters described in design terms, plus the rate-conversion and
// crossfade parameters that accompany them. Filter gains are in decibels; the
// signals these act on are declared in the first section above.

//==
// # Filters

// The response shape of a second-order (biquad) filter section. The peaking
// and shelf shapes carry their gain in decibels; the others have none.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Audio_filter)
type BiquadResponse
    = LowPass
    | HighPass
    | BandPass
    | Notch
    | AllPass
    | PeakingEq(GainDecibels: Number)
    | LowShelf(GainDecibels: Number)
    | HighShelf(GainDecibels: Number);

// A second-order filter section in design terms: the response shape, the
// corner or center Frequency, and the quality factor Q (bandwidth).
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_biquad_filter)
type BiquadFilter
    implements IValue
{
    Response: BiquadResponse;
    Frequency: Frequency;
    Q: Number;
}
```
